title: Komi-san wa Komyushou desu.
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Shoko Komi is admired at school as a cool, beautiful 'ice queen', but in truth her severe social anxiety leaves her unable to speak to anyone. Plain classmate Tadano discovers this and pledges to help her reach her dream of making 100 friends, with help from the outgoing, nonbinary Najimi Osana. AniList ID 86813 is the 2015 one-shot that began the series; this entry describes the serialized series that Viz publishes in English (Komi Can't Communicate).
life_message: Patience, kindness and refusing to judge by appearances help even the shyest person find friends.

content.note: Slow romance (MU); 'a few lewd jokes but no sexual situations' (SLJ).
Social anxiety and loneliness at the core (SLJ; MU Social Anxiety, Loneliness).

dominant: Friendship; overcoming social anxiety; not judging by appearances

frames.aligns: Tadano's patient help for Komi models charity toward the lonely.
frames.concerns: A few lewd jokes; a nonbinary character shown positively may prompt discussion for some families.

frames.aligns: Kindness and friendship without sexual situations (SLJ).
Reaching out to the isolated, a theme of welcome.
frames.concerns: Gender identity of Najimi to discuss.

frames.aligns: Love of neighbor in daily school life.
Putting the best construction on others, as Tadano does with Komi.
Inclusion of an anxious girl and a nonbinary classmate never ostracized (SLJ).
Right speech and compassion for suffering.

frames.concerns: Gender identity presented to young readers.
Gender identity; school festival and holiday chapters to check.

frames.aligns: Worth of each person; nonbinary acceptance.
Harmony among classmates and seasonal school events.
ARC triangle: affinity grows as Tadano patiently builds communication with Komi.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Misunderstandings resolved by patience, not confrontation.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Orderly school life and its customs frame the comedy.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Goal of 100 friends across the whole class (SLJ).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Komi's popularity contrasts with plain Tadano; neither rank matters to friendship.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Learning to express oneself is the arc.

folkways.japan: Classmates reading Komi's silence as dignified reserve reflects Japanese norms that prize composure, and the series plays with 'reading the air'.

delivery.evidence: SLJ: readers 'will learn' about the dangers of assumptions; a conversation starter; lessons carried by gags (to verify).
delivery.note: The lesson about not judging by appearances runs through the running gag of classmates misreading Komi.

winners_losers: Komi and her growing circle of friends win; snap judgments about people are the gentle target.
